context: Request: across the M&A practice (incl. negotiations, JV formations, minority investments), how often signed deals carry a fraud carve-out from indemnification caps and baskets, and which deals. Rubric: 27 qualifying matters (1001-00003 ... 1046-00001), rate 27 of 35 M&A matters (~77%), plus precision.

stages.stage: List files in the document store
stages.note: Whole-store glob; the review flags the cap.

stages.stage: List matter folders
stages.note: declared: List files in the document store (attempt 2). Lists all 266 matter folder names.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Store-wide extraction script times out twice; it reads the partial outputs, counts hits per matter, runs a second scan (~79K chars) and greps the saved output for cap-exception phrases.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Reopened: background store-wide scan with a completion log, polled until done (one poll times out); prints the candidate matter list.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: declared: Read a chosen matter's documents in depth. Reads agreements, memos and a term sheet from five candidate matters.

stages.stage: List files in candidate matters
stages.note: Greps the saved hit list for agreement files, then globs all files of five candidate matters.

stages.stage: Read a chosen matter's documents in depth
stages.note: Reads execution agreements of the listed matters (five guessed paths do not exist), globs for execution files, then snippet scripts pulling the indemnity limitation clauses.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Greps the saved hit list for execution files and runs a store-wide script over agreement-named files printing YES/maybe for fraud language near cap or basket; the review names unopened candidates.

stages.stage: Write the response
stages.note: Writes a rate over six directly verified signed deals; a premature stage_start is refused.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Edits the count to five distinct deals after spotting a duplicate and re-reads.

stages.stage: Finish the run
stages.note: Calls finish.

runs.sequence: List files in the document store → List matter folders → Scan document text with an extraction script → Screen candidate matters by reading documents → List files in candidate matters → Read a chosen matter's documents in depth → Scan document text with an extraction script → Write the response → Check or revise the response → Finish the run
runs.failure_point: Its scans listed nearly every qualifying matter, but it read agreements from a handful and built the rate on five deals, ignoring the YES list its own last scan printed.

first_error.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
first_error.why: Its completed store-wide scan listed almost all qualifying matters, but it chose to read agreements from five candidates only; later scans printed most of the others as matches, yet the review's flag of unopened candidates was not acted on before writing.
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) the review at [105] named several of the unopened qualifying matters.

other_errors.why: The answer counts as qualifying signed deals a tax-credit purchase and a second folder holding a copy of another matter's agreement (evidence seen at [72]-[99]).

runs.failure_point: Its store-wide scan of agreement files reached every qualifying matter, but its follow-up file-name filter and a hand-picked matter list dropped some, and it excluded three it had read as minority, JV or qualified cases.

first_error.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
first_error.why: The scan at [58]-[59] listed every qualifying matter, but its filter to purchase/merger-agreement file names and its hand-picked list of 24 matters dropped two of them, and the answer was built from that list; the review named the hand-picked list and the agent moved on to writing.
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) the review at [80] named the hand-picked list of 24 matters and execution-named files as dropping scanned matters.

other_errors.why: Three matters whose agreements it read (evidence seen at [70]-[78]) are excluded from the rate as a minority financing, a JV contribution and a qualified exception.

The answer counts a membership-interest purchase outside the qualifying set as a full carve-out deal and keeps another as a signed qualified deal; the review flagged the latter and the agent only reclassified it.
other_errors.critic_note: (specific flag) the review at [98] named the added deal as possible over-inclusion; the other was not named.

runs.failure_point: Its co-occurrence scan reached every qualifying matter, but the path filter it built its candidate list from dropped one, and two matters it had checked were left out of the answer while others outside the set were counted.

first_error.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
first_error.why: The co-occurrence scan listed every qualifying matter, but the follow-up path grep kept only certain agreement names and silently dropped one, which never returned to the candidate list; the review named the narrow filter and the later triage repeated the same kind of name filter.
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) the review at [29] named the 94-path filter as risking dropped matters.

other_errors.why: Two matters whose agreements its clause checks printed as matches or that it grepped directly (evidence seen at [103]-[110]) are not in the answer.
The deal table counts a note purchase and two other matters outside the qualifying set as signed deals with the carve-out.

divergence: All three runs failed. Each ran store-wide extraction scans that listed nearly every qualifying matter, then narrowed the set: T0 read agreements from five candidates and built its rate on five deals (surfaced, never opened), ignoring the review's list of unopened candidates; T1 and T2 filtered their scan output by agreement file names (T1 also by a hand-picked matter list) and silently dropped qualifying matters (over-narrow filter); both reviews named the filter, T1 ignored it and T2's later triage repeated it. T1 and T2 also excluded matters they had read and counted non-qualifying ones, so none reached the required rate. The more matters a run carried past the filter, the more criteria it passed (5, 22, 24 of 29).
